open_questions: RV mass and high-resolution imaging to test for a stellar companion on the grazing EB / blended EB scenario
Cause of the 46.8% depth change between sectors (spot crossing + grazing geometry vs dilution/blending)
Why secondary SNR is 3.155 at phase 0.5108 (orbital phase tied to primary or hotspot on EB)
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a short 3.999-hour dip every 13.5 days that looks flat-bottomed, but its duration and fitted impact parameter are too long for this K-dwarf star and the dip depth changes by ~47% between sectors. The size implies about 3 Earth radii, but the shape and duration point to a grazing eclipse on or near the star rather than a planet. A weak dip near half an orbit adds to the stellar-eclipse picture, so the planet explanation is unlikely.

reasons.why: Depth differs markedly between the two sectors (1841 +/-182 ppm in sector 42 vs 2967 +/-237 ppm in sector 92). Sectors are not interchangeable; this is not a calibration offset alone but a genuine change.

Only two sectors are available, each in a different pipeline (SPOC 2-min vs QLP), but the tool classifies as changes_within_a_source, not differs_by_source, so the ~46% depth change is not explained as a steady calibration difference between products.

Transit fit implies a density much lower than the K-dwarf (0.57 Rsun, 0.64 Msun) and impact parameter near 1. Duration is long for b~0.98, inconsistent with a central planet transit. Stellar_radius tool confirms duration_ratio 1.4 with TIC radius 0.57 and 1.37 with Gaia FLAME 0.579 / GSP-Phot 0.583, planet size 2.95-3.02 Rearth, so large duration is not due to a radius error.

Secondary at phase 0.51 is ~13% of dip depth with SNR near threshold and no strong odd_even.diff_sigma 1.017, but xgboost ranks this low (0.21) and the fit + duration + variable depth together favour an eccentric grazing EB/blended EB over a flat-bottom planet. Phase curve provides no large opposite swing.
